The '''2024–25 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Iowa]] during the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. They were led by head coach [[Fran McCaffery]], in his 15th and final season with the Hawkeyes. The team played its home games at [[Carver–Hawkeye Arena]] in [[Iowa City, Iowa]] as a member of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. They finished the season 17–15, 7–13 in [[2024–25 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]], resulting in a tie five-way tie for 12th place. As the No. 15 seed in the [[2025 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they upset [[2024–25 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]] in the first round before losing to [[2024–25 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]] in the second round.

On March 14, 2025, the school fired head coach Fran McCaffery after 15 seasons. He finished with a 297–207 overall record with Iowa.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-14 |title=Iowa fires Fran McCaffery: Longtime coach out after Hawkeyes miss NCAA Tournament for second straight season |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/iowa-fires-fran-mccaffery-longtime-coach-out-after-hawkeyes-miss-ncaa-tournament-for-second-straight-season/ |access-date=2025-03-14 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-14 |title=Sources: Iowa set to dismiss coach McCaffery |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/44251986/sources-iowa-set-dismiss-head-coach-fran-mccaffery |access-date=2025-03-14 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> On March 24, the school named [[Drake Bulldogs men's basketball|Drake]] head coach [[Ben McCollum]] the team's new coach.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-24 |title=Iowa hires Drake's McCollum as hoops coach |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/44384134/sources-iowa-hire-drake-ben-mccollum-head-coach |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Previous season==
The [[2023–24 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Hawkeyes]] finished the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]] 19–15, 10–10 in [[2023–24 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a three-way tie for sixth place. As the No. 7 seed in the [[2024 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they lost to [[2023–24 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]] in the first round.<ref>{{cite news |title=Battle scores 23 second-half points for Ohio State in 90-78 win over Iowa in Big Ten Tournament |url=https://apnews.com/article/ohio-state-iowa-basketball-score-big-ten-12bf9c6aa2f76e66573aad80ed9a2367 |access-date=May 11, 2024 |work=[[AP News]] |date=March 14, 2024}}</ref> The Hawkeyes automatically qualified for the [[2024 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]] as the No. 3 seed where they defeated [[2023–24 Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball team|Kansas State]] in the first round<ref>{{cite web |title=Sandfort's 30 lead Iowa past Kansas State 91-82 in NIT |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401641095 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=May 11, 2024 |date=March 20, 2024}}</ref> before losing to [[2023–24 Utah Utes men's basketball team|Utah]] in the second round.<ref>{{cite web |title=Madsen, Smith power Utah to 91-82 victory over Iowa in NIT |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401641115 |website=ESPN.com |publisher=Associated Press |access-date=May 11, 2024 |date=March 24, 2024}}</ref>
